domain: HealthKit — complete readable data surface for a personally sideloaded iOS quantified-self app (verified July 2026 against developer.apple.com DocC JSON API + iPhoneOS26.5.sdk HealthKit headers). iOS 26.5 is the current shipping SDK; iOS 27 was unveiled at WWDC 2026-06-08 and is in developer beta (beta 4 as of 2026-07-20), public beta mid-July. Header-verified counts (iOS 26.5 HKTypeIdentifiers.h): 120 HKQuantityTypeIdentifier, 70 HKCategoryTypeIdentifier (31 non-symptom + 39 symptom), 6 HKCharacteristicTypeIdentifier, 2 HKCorrelationTypeIdentifier, 2 HKScoredAssessmentTypeIdentifier, 1 HKDocumentTypeIdentifier, 9 HKClinicalTypeIdentifier, 84 HKWorkoutActivityType cases, 71 HKMetadataKey constants, 17 HKObjectType subclasses. iOS 27 beta adds exactly 2 sample-type identifiers (menopausalState, bleedingAfterMenopause) → 72 category types, plus the workout-zones family and time-bound authorization. Zero new quantity types in iOS 27 beta 4.

capabilities.stream: Activity & fitness quantities (35)
capabilities.api: HKQuantityType(_:) with HKQuantityTypeIdentifier: activeEnergyBurned[8.0], appleExerciseTime[9.3], appleMoveTime[14.5], appleStandTime[13.0], basalEnergyBurned[8.0], crossCountrySkiingSpeed[18.0], cyclingCadence[17.0], cyclingFunctionalThresholdPower[17.0], cyclingPower[17.0], cyclingSpeed[17.0], distanceCrossCountrySkiing[18.0], distanceCycling[8.0], distanceDownhillSnowSports[11.2], distancePaddleSports[18.0], distanceRowing[18.0], distanceSkatingSports[18.0], distanceSwimming[10.0], distanceWalkingRunning[8.0], distanceWheelchair[10.0], estimatedWorkoutEffortScore[18.0], flightsClimbed[8.0], nikeFuel[8.0], paddleSportsSpeed[18.0], physicalEffort[17.0], pushCount[10.0], rowingSpeed[18.0], runningGroundContactTime[16.0], runningPower[16.0], runningSpeed[16.0], runningStrideLength[16.0], runningVerticalOscillation[16.0], stepCount[8.0], swimmingStrokeCount[10.0], vo2Max[11.0], workoutEffortScore[18.0]
capabilities.permission: Info.plist NSHealthShareUsageDescription (read) + NSHealthUpdateUsageDescription (write); runtime Health sheet via requestAuthorization(toShare:read:)
capabilities.entitlement: com.apple.developer.healthkit (Boolean) only — no signed special entitlement
capabilities.resolution: stepCount/distance in few-minute buckets from the iPhone motion coprocessor; ~1 Hz during Watch workouts. Running dynamics ~1 Hz during workouts. vo2Max: one estimate per qualifying outdoor walk/run/hike. ObjC constant form is HKQuantityTypeIdentifier<Name>, e.g. HKQuantityTypeIdentifierStepCount — this is also the string that appears in the Health export XML.
capabilities.backfill: Entire store history from first authorization, no API-imposed window — in practice everything since the user's first Health-syncing iOS device. iOS 27 beta adds a user-selectable recent-window-vs-full-history second sheet.
capabilities.notes: WATCH-PRODUCED: appleExerciseTime, appleStandTime, appleMoveTime, activeEnergyBurned, basalEnergyBurned, vo2Max, all running dynamics, swim/ski/row/paddle/skate distance+speed, cycling power/cadence/speed (Watch + BLE sensors), workoutEffortScore, estimatedWorkoutEffortScore. IPHONE-ALONE CAPABLE: stepCount, distanceWalkingRunning, flightsClimbed. nikeFuel is legacy/dead. HealthKit deduplicates overlapping step/distance sources — never naively sum across sources; use HKStatisticsQuery/HKStatisticsCollectionQuery which applies Apple's dedup.

capabilities.stream: Body measurement quantities (7)
capabilities.api: appleSleepingWristTemperature[16.0], bodyFatPercentage[8.0], bodyMass[8.0], bodyMassIndex[8.0], height[8.0], leanBodyMass[8.0], waistCircumference[11.0]
capabilities.resolution: Event-driven (manual entry or smart scale). appleSleepingWristTemperature: one nightly absolute value.
capabilities.notes: appleSleepingWristTemperature is WATCH-ONLY (Series 8+/Ultra), needs Sleep Focus + Track Sleep with Apple Watch and ~5 nights of baseline. HealthKit gives the ABSOLUTE wrist temperature; the Health app's deviation-from-baseline is computed in-app and is not a HealthKit type. The other six are iPhone/manual/third-party-scale.

capabilities.stream: Vital sign quantities (11)
capabilities.api: atrialFibrillationBurden[16.0], bloodPressureDiastolic[8.0], bloodPressureSystolic[8.0], bodyTemperature[8.0], heartRate[8.0], heartRateRecoveryOneMinute[16.0], heartRateVariabilitySDNN[11.0], oxygenSaturation[8.0], respiratoryRate[8.0], restingHeartRate[11.0], walkingHeartRateAverage[11.0]
capabilities.resolution: heartRate ~1 sample/5 min at rest, ~1 Hz during workouts, every few seconds during breathing/sleep. heartRateVariabilitySDNN several per day, dense during Breathe/Mindfulness. restingHeartRate and walkingHeartRateAverage once/day. oxygenSaturation background spot-checks. atrialFibrillationBurden is a weekly percentage estimate requiring AFib History enabled. respiratoryRate is derived during sleep.
capabilities.notes: All Watch-produced except bloodPressureSystolic/Diastolic and bodyTemperature (external cuff/thermometer/manual). US Blood Oxygen note: removed from US Watches by the Masimo ITC ban (Jan 2024), reinstated in redesigned form via iOS 18.6.1/watchOS 11.6.1 (Aug 2025) where the calculation happens on the paired iPhone — so US units write oxygenSaturation with an iPhone sourceRevision. heartRate samples carry HKMetadataKeyHeartRateMotionContext (notSet/sedentary/active) and HKMetadataKeyHeartRateSensorLocation — the only reliable way to separate resting-context beats. heartRateRecoveryOneMinute carries HKMetadataKeyHeartRateRecoveryTestType/ActivityType/ActivityDuration/MaxObservedRecoveryHeartRate.

capabilities.stream: Nutrition quantities (39)
capabilities.api: dietaryBiotin, dietaryCaffeine, dietaryCalcium, dietaryCarbohydrates, dietaryChloride, dietaryCholesterol, dietaryChromium, dietaryCopper, dietaryEnergyConsumed, dietaryFatMonounsaturated, dietaryFatPolyunsaturated, dietaryFatSaturated, dietaryFatTotal, dietaryFiber, dietaryFolate, dietaryIodine, dietaryIron, dietaryMagnesium, dietaryManganese, dietaryMolybdenum, dietaryNiacin, dietaryPantothenicAcid, dietaryPhosphorus, dietaryPotassium, dietaryProtein, dietaryRiboflavin, dietarySelenium, dietarySodium, dietarySugar, dietaryThiamin, dietaryVitaminA, dietaryVitaminB12, dietaryVitaminB6, dietaryVitaminC, dietaryVitaminD, dietaryVitaminE, dietaryVitaminK, dietaryZinc (all 8.0), dietaryWater[9.0]
capabilities.resolution: Event-driven, entirely user/third-party entered. Grouped into meals via HKCorrelationTypeIdentifier.food with HKMetadataKeyFoodType.
capabilities.notes: iPhone/iPad only — the Watch produces none. Apple ships no first-party food logger, so this family is empty unless MyFitnessPal/Cronometer/Lose It writes to Health.

capabilities.stream: Lab & test-result quantities (9)
capabilities.api: bloodGlucose[8.0], electrodermalActivity[8.0], forcedExpiratoryVolume1[8.0], forcedVitalCapacity[8.0], inhalerUsage[8.0], insulinDelivery[11.0], numberOfTimesFallen[8.0], peakExpiratoryFlowRate[8.0], peripheralPerfusionIndex[8.0]
capabilities.resolution: Device/event driven. CGMs (Dexcom/Libre) write bloodGlucose every 1-5 min. numberOfTimesFallen written by Watch Fall Detection.
capabilities.notes: numberOfTimesFallen is one of the ten types allowed HKUpdateFrequency.immediate on watchOS. bloodGlucose carries HKMetadataKeyBloodGlucoseMealTime; insulinDelivery carries HKMetadataKeyInsulinDeliveryReason (basal/bolus). electrodermalActivity has no Apple-hardware producer — the Watch has no EDA sensor. Only Watch-produced member: numberOfTimesFallen.

capabilities.stream: Mobility / gait quantities (8)
capabilities.api: appleWalkingSteadiness[15.0], sixMinuteWalkTestDistance[14.0], stairAscentSpeed[14.0], stairDescentSpeed[14.0], walkingAsymmetryPercentage[14.0], walkingDoubleSupportPercentage[14.0], walkingSpeed[14.0], walkingStepLength[14.0]
capabilities.entitlement: com.apple.developer.healthkit for read; com.apple.developer.healthkit.recalibrate-estimates ONLY to call recalibrateEstimates(sampleType:date:) on sixMinuteWalkTestDistance/appleWalkingSteadiness
capabilities.resolution: Derived on-device from iPhone motion; several samples/day when the phone is carried in a pocket. sixMinuteWalkTestDistance one estimate/day. appleWalkingSteadiness classified by HKAppleWalkingSteadinessClassification (ok/low/veryLow).
capabilities.notes: IPHONE-produced, not Watch — the phone must be carried near the waist/pocket. Requires Health > Mobility set up with date of birth, height, weight. Check HKSampleType.allowsRecalibrationForEstimates first. 'HealthKit Estimate Recalibration' is its own row in Apple's supported-capabilities-ios table and IS marked available on the free tier.

capabilities.stream: Hearing & audio-exposure quantities (3)
capabilities.api: environmentalAudioExposure[13.0], environmentalSoundReduction[16.0], headphoneAudioExposure[13.0]
capabilities.resolution: Rolling dBA exposure segments, many per hour while audio plays or the Watch Noise app samples ambient sound.
capabilities.notes: environmentalAudioExposure = Watch microphone (Noise app must be enabled). headphoneAudioExposure = iPhone/iPad with AirPods or any BT/wired output; carries HKMetadataKeyAudioExposureLevel, HKMetadataKeyAudioExposureDuration, HKMetadataKeyHeadphoneGain. environmentalSoundReduction[16.0] is AirPods Pro/Max ANC/Transparency attenuation in dB — the only AirPods-specific quantity in HealthKit. AirPods hearing-test results land as HKAudiogramSample, not here. The three matching category event types are .immediate-eligible on watchOS.

capabilities.stream: UV, daylight, diving and alcohol quantities (6)
capabilities.api: timeInDaylight[17.0], uvExposure[9.0], underwaterDepth[16.0], waterTemperature[16.0], bloodAlcoholContent[8.0], numberOfAlcoholicBeverages[15.0]
capabilities.resolution: timeInDaylight aggregated to minute-granularity daily buckets. underwaterDepth/waterTemperature ~1 Hz during a dive.
capabilities.notes: timeInDaylight requires the ambient-light sensor on Apple Watch SE 2 / Series 6+ — iPhone alone does NOT produce it. underwaterDepth and waterTemperature require Apple Watch Ultra (depth gauge); Ultra also writes HKMetadataKeyWaterSalinity. uvExposure has NO Apple producer at all — third-party/manual only. Both alcohol types are manual/third-party only.

capabilities.stream: Sleep-breathing and reproductive quantities (2)
capabilities.api: appleSleepingBreathingDisturbances[18.0], basalBodyTemperature[9.0]
capabilities.resolution: appleSleepingBreathingDisturbances: one value per sleep session, classified by HKAppleSleepingBreathingDisturbancesClassification (notElevated / elevated).
capabilities.notes: appleSleepingBreathingDisturbances is WATCH-ONLY (Series 9+/Ultra 2+, watchOS 11) and is the raw input to Apple's Sleep Apnea Notifications. It is not linked from Apple's own HKQuantityTypeIdentifier landing page — it appears only in the generated 'Type Properties' section. basalBodyTemperature is manual/third-party thermometer.

capabilities.stream: Category (event/state) types, non-symptom — 31 in iOS 26.5, 33 in iOS 27 beta
capabilities.api: HKCategoryType(_:) with HKCategoryTypeIdentifier: appleStandHour[9.0/w2.0], appleWalkingSteadinessEvent[15.0/w8.0], audioExposureEvent[13.0 DEPRECATED->environmentalAudioExposureEvent], bleedingAfterPregnancy[18.0/w11.0], bleedingDuringPregnancy[18.0/w11.0], cervicalMucusQuality[9.0], contraceptive[14.3], environmentalAudioExposureEvent[14.0/w7.0], handwashingEvent[14.0/w7.0], headphoneAudioExposureEvent[14.2/w7.1], highHeartRateEvent[12.2/w5.2], hypertensionEvent[26.2/w26.2], infrequentMenstrualCycles[16.0], intermenstrualBleeding[9.0], irregularHeartRhythmEvent[12.2/w5.2], irregularMenstrualCycles[16.0], lactation[14.3], lowCardioFitnessEvent[14.3/w7.2], lowHeartRateEvent[12.2/w5.2], menstrualFlow[9.0], mindfulSession[10.0/w3.0], ovulationTestResult[9.0], persistentIntermenstrualBleeding[16.0], pregnancy[14.3], pregnancyTestResult[15.0], progesteroneTestResult[15.0], prolongedMenstrualPeriods[16.0], sexualActivity[9.0], sleepAnalysis[8.0/w2.0], sleepApneaEvent[18.0/w11.0], toothbrushingEvent[13.0/w6.0]; iOS 27 beta adds menopausalState[27.0] and bleedingAfterMenopause[27.0]
capabilities.resolution: Interval samples with an integer value enum. sleepAnalysis has 6 values: inBed, asleepUnspecified, awake, asleepCore, asleepDeep, asleepREM (stages added iOS 16). Other value enums: HKCategoryValueAppleStandHour(stood/idle), HKCategoryValueSeverity(unspecified/notPresent/mild/moderate/severe), HKCategoryValuePresence(present/notPresent), HKCategoryValueMenstrualFlow(unspecified/light/medium/heavy), HKCategoryValueVaginalBleeding(unspecified/light/medium/heavy/none), HKCategoryValueCervicalMucusQuality(dry/sticky/creamy/watery/eggWhite), HKCategoryValueOvulationTestResult(negative/luteinizingHormoneSurge/indeterminate), HKCategoryValuePregnancyTestResult, HKCategoryValueProgesteroneTestResult, HKCategoryValueContraceptive(7), HKCategoryValueAppleWalkingSteadinessEvent(4), HKCategoryValueEnvironmentalAudioExposureEvent(momentaryLimit), HKCategoryValueHeadphoneAudioExposureEvent(sevenDayLimit), HKCategoryValueLowCardioFitnessEvent(lowFitness), HKCategoryValueMenopausalState(none/perimenopause/menopause, iOS 27 beta).
capabilities.notes: THREE are real symbols in HKTypeIdentifiers.h but appear NOWHERE in Apple's documentation navigation or the DocC navigator index — sleepApneaEvent, bleedingDuringPregnancy, bleedingAfterPregnancy (all iOS 18.0/watchOS 11.0). Their doc pages exist only by direct URL. Any enumeration built from Apple's docs pages misses them. WATCH-PRODUCED: appleStandHour, highHeartRateEvent, lowHeartRateEvent, irregularHeartRhythmEvent, lowCardioFitnessEvent, sleepApneaEvent, hypertensionEvent, environmentalAudioExposureEvent, handwashingEvent, mindfulSession, and sleepAnalysis stages (iPhone alone yields inBed only). IPHONE-PRODUCED: appleWalkingSteadinessEvent, headphoneAudioExposureEvent, toothbrushingEvent, all cycle-tracking types. .immediate-eligible on watchOS: highHeartRateEvent, lowHeartRateEvent, irregularHeartRhythmEvent, environmentalAudioExposureEvent, headphoneAudioExposureEvent, lowCardioFitnessEvent, handwashingEvent, toothbrushingEvent.

capabilities.stream: Category types — Symptoms (39)
capabilities.api: HKCategoryTypeIdentifier: abdominalCramps, acne, appetiteChanges, bladderIncontinence, bloating, breastPain, chestTightnessOrPain, chills, constipation, coughing, diarrhea, dizziness, drySkin, fainting, fatigue, fever, generalizedBodyAche, hairLoss, headache, heartburn, hotFlashes, lossOfSmell, lossOfTaste, lowerBackPain, memoryLapse, moodChanges, nausea, nightSweats, pelvicPain, rapidPoundingOrFlutteringHeartbeat, runnyNose, shortnessOfBreath, sinusCongestion, skippedHeartbeat, sleepChanges, soreThroat, vaginalDryness, vomiting, wheezing (iOS 13.6 or 14.0; all watchOS 7.0)
capabilities.resolution: Manual only. Value is HKCategoryValueSeverity (unspecified/notPresent/mild/moderate/severe), except appetiteChanges which uses HKCategoryValueAppetiteChanges (unspecified/noChange/decreased/increased), and a few binary ones using HKCategoryValuePresence.
capabilities.notes: 100% user-entered — no sensor produces these. They live on a separate 'Symptom Type Identifiers' article page rather than the HKCategoryTypeIdentifier landing page, which is why most published HealthKit enumerations omit all 39.

capabilities.stream: Characteristic types (6) — static profile facts
capabilities.api: HKCharacteristicType(_:) plus dedicated getters dateOfBirthComponents(), biologicalSex(), bloodType(), fitzpatrickSkinType(), wheelchairUse(), activityMoveMode(). Identifiers: activityMoveMode[14.0], biologicalSex[8.0], bloodType[8.0], dateOfBirth[8.0], fitzpatrickSkinType[9.0], wheelchairUse[10.0]
capabilities.permission: NSHealthShareUsageDescription only — this family is read-only, you cannot write characteristics
capabilities.resolution: Synchronous getters, not queries. Values: HKBiologicalSex(notSet/female/male/other), HKBloodType(notSet + 8 ABO/Rh combinations), HKFitzpatrickSkinType(notSet/I-VI), HKWheelchairUse(notSet/no/yes), HKActivityMoveMode(activeEnergy/appleMoveTime).
capabilities.backfill: none — current value only, no history
capabilities.notes: Not an HKSampleType, so no HKObserverQuery and no background delivery. This is the ONE family where read denial is positively detectable: the getters throw HKError.errorAuthorizationDenied because there is no empty result set to hide behind. Also note the Health app EXPORT emits a seventh characteristic on the <Me> element, HKCharacteristicTypeIdentifierCardioFitnessMedicationsUse, which has NO API counterpart in any SDK.

capabilities.stream: Correlation types (2) — blood pressure and food
capabilities.api: HKCorrelationType(_:) -> HKCorrelationTypeIdentifier.bloodPressure[8.0], .food[8.0]; query with HKCorrelationQuery
capabilities.resolution: Container samples grouping child HKQuantitySamples — systolic+diastolic, or a meal's full nutrient set.
capabilities.notes: Authorization is per CHILD type, not per correlation — you must request bloodPressureSystolic AND bloodPressureDiastolic. Children also exist independently as top-level samples, so a naive 'query everything' double-counts nutrition and blood pressure.

capabilities.stream: Workouts, 84 activity types, per-workout statistics/events/activities
capabilities.api: HKObjectType.workoutType() / HKWorkoutType; HKWorkout (workoutActivityType, duration, totalDistance, totalEnergyBurned, statistics(for:), workoutEvents, workoutActivities[17.0]). HKWorkoutActivityType 84 cases: americanFootball, archery, australianFootball, badminton, barre, baseball, basketball, bowling, boxing, cardioDance, climbing, cooldown, coreTraining, cricket, crossCountrySkiing, crossTraining, curling, cycling, dance(DEPR), danceInspiredTraining(DEPR), discSports, downhillSkiing, elliptical, equestrianSports, fencing, fishing, fitnessGaming, flexibility, functionalStrengthTraining, golf, gymnastics, handCycling, handball, highIntensityIntervalTraining, hiking, hockey, hunting, jumpRope, kickboxing, lacrosse, martialArts, mindAndBody, mixedCardio, mixedMetabolicCardioTraining(DEPR), other, paddleSports, pickleball, pilates, play, preparationAndRecovery, racquetball, rowing, rugby, running, sailing, skatingSports, snowSports, snowboarding, soccer, socialDance, softball, squash, stairClimbing, stairs, stepTraining, surfingSports, swimBikeRun, swimming, tableTennis, taiChi, tennis, trackAndField, traditionalStrengthTraining, transition, underwaterDiving, volleyball, walking, waterFitness, waterPolo, waterSports, wheelchairRunPace, wheelchairWalkPace, wrestling, yoga
capabilities.permission: NSHealthShareUsageDescription + runtime Health sheet (workoutType is a single checkbox)
capabilities.resolution: One HKWorkout per session carrying HKStatistics per quantity type, an HKWorkoutEvent list (pause/resume/lap/segment/marker/motionPaused/motionResumed), and from iOS 17 nested HKWorkoutActivity intervals for multisport/interval training.
capabilities.notes: Three deprecated cases (dance, danceInspiredTraining, mixedMetabolicCardioTraining) still appear in historical data — parse them, do not offer them. Apple's docs also list two nav-only stubs 'HKWorkoutActivityTypeGroup' and 'HKWorkoutActivityTypeRest' with null platform metadata; neither exists in HKWorkout.h in the iOS 26.5 SDK, so treat them as doc artifacts, not real cases. Rich per-workout metadata: HKMetadataKeyIndoorWorkout, WeatherCondition/Temperature/Humidity, ElevationAscended/Descended, AverageMETs, SWOLFScore, LapLength, SwimmingStrokeStyle, SwimmingLocationType, AlpineSlopeGrade, AverageSpeed/MaximumSpeed, FitnessMachineDuration, IndoorBikeDistance, CrossTrainerDistance, AppleFitnessPlusCatalogIdentifier/Session, GroupFitness, CoachedWorkout, WorkoutBrandName.

capabilities.stream: Workout route — full GPS track (HKSeriesType)
capabilities.api: HKSeriesType.workoutRoute() (HKWorkoutRouteTypeIdentifier); HKWorkoutRoute sample; HKWorkoutRouteQuery delivers [CLLocation] in batches
capabilities.permission: NSHealthShareUsageDescription plus the workoutRoute toggle in the Health sheet. Notably NO CoreLocation permission and no NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription are required — the coordinates come out of HealthKit, not Core Location.
capabilities.resolution: ~1 Hz CLLocation fixes with latitude, longitude, altitude, horizontal/vertical accuracy, speed, course and timestamp — a full-fidelity GPS trace of every outdoor workout ever recorded.
capabilities.backfill: every outdoor workout in the store's history
capabilities.notes: The single most privacy-dense stream in HealthKit, and it needs nothing but the base free-team entitlement plus the ordinary Health sheet. Produced by Apple Watch GPS or an iPhone carried during the workout. HKWorkoutRouteQuery hands back batches — keep calling until done == true.

capabilities.stream: Heartbeat series — raw beat-to-beat R-R intervals (HKSeriesType)
capabilities.api: HKSeriesType.heartbeatSeries() (HKDataTypeIdentifierHeartbeatSeries); HKHeartbeatSeriesSample; HKHeartbeatSeriesQuery yielding (timeSinceSeriesStart, precededByGap)
capabilities.resolution: Individual heartbeat timestamps at sub-millisecond resolution with a precededByGap flag — this is raw R-R interval data from which you can compute RMSSD, pNN50, SDNN, LF/HF and any other HRV metric Apple does not publish.
capabilities.notes: APPLE WATCH ONLY. Written alongside heartRateVariabilitySDNN samples during Breathe/Mindfulness and background HRV reads. This is the highest-value non-obvious stream for a quantified-self app: HealthKit surfaces only SDNN, but the beat series lets you derive the entire HRV literature yourself. It is NOT present in usable form in the Health app XML export.

capabilities.stream: Quantity series — high-frequency intra-sample data
capabilities.api: HKQuantitySeriesSampleQuery (iOS 12; includeSample and orderByQuantitySampleStartDate options iOS 13); HKCumulativeQuantitySeriesSample
capabilities.permission: NSHealthShareUsageDescription for the underlying quantity type
capabilities.resolution: Expands a single summary quantity sample into its constituent datum stream — e.g. an hour-long cyclingPower sample into its per-second values.
capabilities.notes: Widely missed. HKSampleQuery alone returns pre-aggregated samples; running HKQuantitySeriesSampleQuery over the same sample yields far denser data for series-backed types (cyclingPower, runningPower, underwaterDepth and others).

capabilities.stream: Electrocardiogram with full voltage waveform
capabilities.api: HKObjectType.electrocardiogramType() / HKElectrocardiogramType; HKElectrocardiogram (classification, averageHeartRate, samplingFrequency, numberOfVoltageMeasurements, symptomsStatus); HKElectrocardiogramQuery yielding one HKQuantity voltage per measurement
capabilities.permission: NSHealthShareUsageDescription plus a distinct 'Electrocardiograms' toggle in the Health sheet
capabilities.entitlement: com.apple.developer.healthkit ONLY — no special entitlement and no health-records; read-only, ECGs cannot be written
capabilities.resolution: ~512 Hz single-lead (HKElectrocardiogramLead.appleWatchSimilarToLeadI), 30 s per recording, so roughly 15,360 microvolt samples. classification: notSet, sinusRhythm, atrialFibrillation, inconclusiveLowHeartRate, inconclusiveHighHeartRate, inconclusivePoorReading, inconclusiveOther, unrecognized. symptomsStatus: notSet, none, present. Metadata HKMetadataKeyAppleECGAlgorithmVersion.
capabilities.backfill: every ECG ever recorded on the paired Watch
capabilities.notes: Apple Watch Series 4+ / Ultra. Commonly assumed to require a special entitlement — it does not. Voltage arrives one measurement at a time through the query handler, so expect ~15k callbacks per ECG; batch them. When symptomsStatus == .present the actual symptoms are stored as separate symptom category samples correlated by time, not as properties on the ECG object.

capabilities.stream: Audiogram — hearing test results
capabilities.api: HKObjectType.audiogramSampleType() / HKAudiogramSampleType; HKAudiogramSample.sensitivityPoints -> HKAudiogramSensitivityPoint(frequency, tests) -> HKAudiogramSensitivityTest(sensitivity, type: HKAudiogramConductionType, masked, side: HKAudiogramSensitivityTestSide, clampingRange: HKAudiogramSensitivityPointClampingRange)[18.1]
capabilities.resolution: Per-ear dB HL threshold at each tested frequency, typically 250-8000 Hz.
capabilities.notes: This is the direct HealthKit payoff of owning AirPods: the AirPods Pro 2+ Hearing Test (iOS 18+) writes here, as do Mimi/SonicCloud and imported clinical audiometry. iOS 18.1 added HKAudiogramSensitivityPointClampingRange so you can distinguish a true threshold from one clipped at the test's floor or ceiling.

capabilities.stream: State of Mind — mood and emotion (iOS 18)
capabilities.api: HKObjectType.stateOfMindType() / HKStateOfMindType; HKStateOfMind(kind, valence, valenceClassification, labels, associations)
capabilities.permission: NSHealthShareUsageDescription plus its own 'State of Mind' toggle in the Health sheet
capabilities.resolution: kind: momentaryEmotion or dailyMood. valence: continuous Double in [-1.0, +1.0]. valenceClassification (7): veryUnpleasant, unpleasant, slightlyUnpleasant, neutral, slightlyPleasant, pleasant, veryPleasant. labels (38): amazed, amused, angry, annoyed, anxious, ashamed, brave, calm, confident, content, disappointed, discouraged, disgusted, drained, embarrassed, excited, frustrated, grateful, guilty, happy, hopeful, hopeless, indifferent, irritated, jealous, joyful, lonely, overwhelmed, passionate, peaceful, proud, relieved, sad, satisfied, scared, stressed, surprised, worried. associations (18): community, currentEvents, dating, education, family, fitness, friends, health, hobbies, identity, money, partner, selfCare, spirituality, tasks, travel, weather, work.
capabilities.backfill: full store history back to whenever the user first logged in Health or Mindfulness
capabilities.notes: Entirely user-logged via Health > Mental Wellbeing or the Watch Mindfulness app, and fully readable AND writable by a third-party app with only the base entitlement. Apple's HKStateOfMind doc page is thin — the 38 labels, 18 associations and 7 valence classifications come from HKStateOfMind.h in the SDK, not from the website.

capabilities.stream: Scored clinical assessments — GAD-7 and PHQ-9 (iOS 18)
capabilities.api: HKObjectType.scoredAssessmentType(_:) / HKScoredAssessmentType; HKScoredAssessmentTypeIdentifier.gad7 (HKScoredAssessmentTypeIdentifierGAD7) and .phq9 (HKScoredAssessmentTypeIdentifierPHQ9); concrete samples HKGAD7Assessment(score, risk: HKGAD7AssessmentRisk) and HKPHQ9Assessment(score, risk: HKPHQ9AssessmentRisk)
capabilities.entitlement: com.apple.developer.healthkit only — no health-records entitlement despite these being validated clinical instruments
capabilities.resolution: One sample per completed questionnaire: integer total score, per-item answers, and a risk band enum (PHQ-9: none/mild/moderate/moderatelySevere/severe; GAD-7: noneToMinimal/mild/moderate/severe).
capabilities.notes: iPhone/iPad only, via Health > Mental Wellbeing > Take an Assessment. Apple's HKScoredAssessmentTypeIdentifier landing page lists NO type properties at all — gad7 and phq9 resolve only by direct URL or from HKTypeIdentifiers.h. The header's macCatalyst 17.0 / macOS 14.0 availability is inconsistent with the iOS 18.0 gate; trust iOS 18.0.

capabilities.stream: Vision prescription — glasses and contacts (PER-OBJECT authorization)
capabilities.api: HKObjectType.visionPrescriptionType() returns HKPrescriptionType (the class); HKVisionPrescription sample with prescriptionType: HKVisionPrescriptionType enum {glasses, contacts}, dateIssued, expirationDate, plus HKGlassesLensSpecification / HKContactsLensSpecification (sphere, cylinder, axis, add, vertexDistance, prism via HKVisionPrism, baseCurve, diameter); authorize with HKHealthStore.requestPerObjectReadAuthorization(for:predicate:)
capabilities.permission: NSHealthShareUsageDescription plus a PER-SAMPLE authorization sheet where the user ticks individual prescriptions — re-prompted on every call
capabilities.resolution: Event-driven; one sample per prescription the user photographs or enters in Health.
capabilities.backfill: only the specific samples the user individually grants, plus anything your own app wrote
capabilities.notes: TRAP: passing visionPrescriptionType to the ordinary requestAuthorization(toShare:read:) FAILS with HKError.errorInvalidArgument. You must use requestPerObjectReadAuthorization, and the system shows the sheet every time regardless of prior grants. It IS an HKSampleType so observer queries compile and background delivery is technically enabled, but new samples are rare and user-entered. Do not conflate HKPrescriptionType (the object type class) with HKVisionPrescriptionType (the 2-case glasses/contacts enum). Metadata: HKMetadataKeyGlassesPrescriptionDescription.

capabilities.stream: Clinical records (FHIR) — allergies, conditions, immunizations, labs, medications, procedures, vitals, coverage, notes
capabilities.api: HKClinicalType(_:) with HKClinicalTypeIdentifier: allergyRecord[12.0], clinicalNoteRecord[16.4], conditionRecord[12.0], coverageRecord[14.0], immunizationRecord[12.0], labResultRecord[12.0], medicationRecord[12.0], procedureRecord[12.0], vitalSignRecord[12.0]. Samples are HKClinicalRecord with .fhirResource (HKFHIRResource: resourceType, identifier, data as raw FHIR JSON, fhirVersion via HKFHIRVersion / HKFHIRRelease) and .clinicalCodings (HKClinicalCoding).
capabilities.permission: NSHealthClinicalHealthRecordsShareUsageDescription — a DIFFERENT Info.plist key from NSHealthShareUsageDescription — plus a separate Health Records authorization sheet. Optionally NSHealthRequiredReadAuthorizationTypeIdentifiers to declare required types (Apple requires three or more, else authorization fails with errorRequiredAuthorizationDenied and does not say which type was denied).
capabilities.entitlement: com.apple.developer.healthkit.access = ["health-records"] is REQUIRED, and health-records is the ONLY legal value of that key. Set by the 'Clinical Health Records' checkbox under the HealthKit capability in Xcode.
capabilities.resolution: Full raw FHIR DSTU2/R4 JSON per record — labs with LOINC codes, values, units and reference ranges; medications with RxNorm; conditions and procedures with SNOMED/ICD. Genuine EHR data, not a summary.
capabilities.backfill: everything the user's connected providers have released, frequently years of lab history
capabilities.notes: THE ENTITLEMENT RISK ON A FREE APPLE ID. Apple's supported-capabilities-ios table lists 'HealthKit' and 'HealthKit Estimate Recalibration' with a check in the free 'Apple Developer' column, but Clinical Health Records / health-records is NOT a row in that table at all, so its free-tier signability is unestablished rather than merely undocumented. HKClinicalType is an HKSampleType so observer queries compile, but records only refresh when the Health app syncs with the provider and background delivery on clinical types is not documented as supported. Requires the user to have linked a hospital in Health > Browse > Health Records. Related: HKVerifiableClinicalRecord[15.4] for SMART Health Cards and EU Digital COVID Certificates, read via HKVerifiableClinicalRecordQuery, source types HKVerifiableClinicalRecordSourceTypeSMARTHealthCard and ...EUDigitalCOVIDCertificate, credential types covid19/immunization/laboratory — that one has its own separate consent flow.

capabilities.stream: CDA clinical documents
capabilities.api: HKObjectType.documentType(HKDocumentTypeIdentifier.CDA) / HKDocumentType; HKCDADocumentSample (title, patientName, authorName, custodianName, documentData raw XML); HKDocumentQuery
capabilities.permission: NSHealthShareUsageDescription + runtime Health sheet; documentData is only populated when you pass includeDocumentData: true AND the user consented
capabilities.entitlement: com.apple.developer.healthkit (Apple documents CDA under the general HealthKit capability, though in practice these arrive through the same Health Records pipeline)
capabilities.resolution: Whole HL7 CDA XML documents — visit summaries, discharge summaries.
capabilities.notes: Exactly ONE document type identifier exists: HKDocumentTypeIdentifierCDA. HKDocumentQuery is one-shot with no update handler, so there is no incremental sync path. Rarely populated on consumer devices.

capabilities.stream: Activity summaries — Move / Exercise / Stand rings and their goals
capabilities.api: HKObjectType.activitySummaryType() / HKActivitySummaryType; HKActivitySummary(activeEnergyBurned, activeEnergyBurnedGoal, appleMoveTime, appleMoveTimeGoal, appleExerciseTime, exerciseTimeGoal[16.0], appleStandHours, standHoursGoal[16.0], activityMoveMode[14.0], isPaused[18.0]); HKActivitySummaryQuery which has an updateHandler
capabilities.permission: NSHealthShareUsageDescription plus its own activitySummaryType toggle in the Health sheet
capabilities.resolution: One summary per calendar day including the GOALS — which are not derivable from any sample type.
capabilities.backfill: every day since the Watch was first paired
capabilities.notes: HKActivitySummaryType is HKObjectType but NOT HKSampleType, so HKObserverQuery and enableBackgroundDelivery do not apply — HKActivitySummaryQuery.updateHandler only fires while your app is running. Query with an NSPredicate on HKPredicateKeyPathDateComponents built from an explicit NSCalendar with the correct era and timezone, or you silently get zero results. isPaused[18.0] reflects watchOS 11 ring pausing. Never skip this family: the exercise-time and stand-hours goals exist nowhere else in HealthKit.

capabilities.stream: Medications — dose events and tracked medication list (NEW in iOS 26)
capabilities.api: HKObjectType.medicationDoseEventType() / HKMedicationDoseEventType; HKMedicationDoseEvent(scheduleType, logStatus, medicationConceptIdentifier, scheduledDate). HKObjectType.userAnnotatedMedicationType() / HKUserAnnotatedMedicationType; HKUserAnnotatedMedication(nickname, isArchived, hasSchedule, medication: HKMedicationConcept) read via HKUserAnnotatedMedicationQuery. HKMedicationConcept + HKHealthConceptIdentifier(domain: HKHealthConceptDomainMedication). HKMedicationGeneralForm 18 values: capsule, cream, device, drops, foam, gel, inhaler, injection, liquid, lotion, ointment, patch, powder, spray, suppository, tablet, topical, unknown.
capabilities.entitlement: com.apple.developer.healthkit only — notably NOT health-records, despite the clinical overlap
capabilities.resolution: One sample per dose slot. HKMedicationDoseEventLogStatus (6): notInteracted, notificationNotSent, snoozed, taken, skipped, notLogged. HKMedicationDoseEventScheduleType (2): asNeeded, schedule. Predicate key paths HKUserAnnotatedMedicationPredicateKeyPathIsArchived and ...HasSchedule.
capabilities.backfill: back to whenever the user started using Health > Medications (feature shipped iOS 16; API exposure is new in iOS 26)
capabilities.notes: The headline iOS 26 HealthKit addition and the one most third-party enumerations still miss entirely. HKMedicationDoseEvent IS an HKSampleType so observer queries and background delivery work on it; HKUserAnnotatedMedicationType is HKObjectType only, so you cannot be woken when the medication LIST changes. The system explicitly generates notInteracted rows for untouched reminder slots, which means you get true adherence denominators rather than only positive logs.

capabilities.stream: Sample metadata — 71 HKMetadataKey constants, the hidden second data layer
capabilities.api: HKObject.metadata dictionary. Keys: HKMetadataKeyDeviceSerialNumber, BodyTemperatureSensorLocation, HeartRateSensorLocation, HeartRateMotionContext, UserMotionContext, SessionEstimate, HeartRateRecoveryTestType, HeartRateRecoveryActivityType, HeartRateRecoveryActivityDuration, HeartRateRecoveryMaxObservedRecoveryHeartRate, FoodType, UDIDeviceIdentifier, UDIProductionIdentifier, DigitalSignature, ExternalUUID, SyncIdentifier, SyncVersion, TimeZone, DeviceName, DeviceManufacturerName, WasTakenInLab, ReferenceRangeLowerLimit, ReferenceRangeUpperLimit, WasUserEntered, WorkoutBrandName, GroupFitness, AppleFitnessPlusCatalogIdentifier, AppleFitnessPlusSession, IndoorWorkout, CoachedWorkout, WeatherCondition, WeatherTemperature, WeatherHumidity, SexualActivityProtectionUsed, MenstrualCycleStart, LapLength, SwimmingLocationType, SwimmingStrokeStyle, InsulinDeliveryReason, BloodGlucoseMealTime, VO2MaxTestType, AverageSpeed, MaximumSpeed, AlpineSlopeGrade, ElevationAscended, ElevationDescended, FitnessMachineDuration, IndoorBikeDistance, CrossTrainerDistance, HeartRateEventThreshold, AverageMETs, AudioExposureLevel, AudioExposureDuration, AppleECGAlgorithmVersion, DevicePlacementSide, BarometricPressure, AppleDeviceCalibrated, VO2MaxValue, LowCardioFitnessEventThreshold, DateOfEarliestDataUsedForEstimate, AlgorithmVersion, SWOLFScore, QuantityClampedToLowerBound, QuantityClampedToUpperBound, GlassesPrescriptionDescription, WaterSalinity, HeadphoneGain, CyclingFunctionalThresholdPowerTestType, ActivityType, PhysicalEffortEstimationType, MaximumLightIntensity
capabilities.permission: none beyond the parent sample's authorization — metadata rides free on any sample you can read
capabilities.resolution: Per-sample dictionary. Backing enums in HKMetadataEnums.h: HKAppleECGAlgorithmVersion, HKBloodGlucoseMealTime, HKBodyTemperatureSensorLocation, HKCyclingFunctionalThresholdPowerTestType, HKDevicePlacementSide, HKHeartRateMotionContext, HKHeartRateRecoveryTestType, HKHeartRateSensorLocation, HKInsulinDeliveryReason, HKPhysicalEffortEstimationType, HKSwimmingStrokeStyle, HKUserMotionContext, HKVO2MaxTestType, HKWaterSalinity, HKWeatherCondition, HKWorkoutSwimmingLocationType.
capabilities.notes: Enormously under-used and free. HKMetadataKeyWasUserEntered separates sensor truth from typed-in guesses. HKMetadataKeyBarometricPressure gives ambient pressure on workouts. WeatherCondition/Temperature/Humidity gives free weather history for every outdoor workout. DeviceSerialNumber + UDI identify the exact hardware. QuantityClampedToUpperBound/LowerBound tells you a value hit a sensor ceiling and is not a real reading — critical for not treating clipped data as signal.

capabilities.stream: Sample provenance — device and source revision
capabilities.api: HKObject.device -> HKDevice(name, manufacturer, model, hardwareVersion, firmwareVersion, softwareVersion, localIdentifier, udiDeviceIdentifier); HKObject.sourceRevision -> HKSourceRevision(source: HKSource(name, bundleIdentifier), version, productType, operatingSystemVersion); HKSourceQuery to enumerate every app or device that ever wrote a given type; HKQuery.predicateForObjects(from:) and predicateForObjects(withDeviceProperty:allowedValues:)
capabilities.permission: none beyond the parent sample's authorization
capabilities.resolution: Per-sample provenance.
capabilities.notes: This is how you answer 'iPhone or Watch, and which model' at the sample level — far more reliable than inferring from the type. Run HKSourceQuery first to build a source inventory before deciding what to sync; it is the cheapest way to discover which third-party apps have been writing into the store.

capabilities.stream: Sample attachments — arbitrary files bound to samples
capabilities.api: HKAttachmentStore(healthStore:); getAttachments(for: HKObject); HKAttachment(identifier, name, contentType: UTType, size, createdDate, metadata); dataReader -> HKAttachmentDataReader, an AsyncSequence of bytes
capabilities.resolution: Arbitrary binary blobs (PDFs, images) attached to a HealthKit sample.
capabilities.notes: Almost nobody knows this API exists. Not represented in the Health app export at all.

capabilities.stream: Workout heart-rate and power zones (iOS 27 BETA)
capabilities.api: HKWorkoutZone(index, minimum, maximum); HKWorkoutZoneConfiguration(quantityType, zones, source: .app/.system/.user); HKWorkoutZoneGroup(configuration, zoneDurations); HKWorkoutZoneDuration(zone, duration); HKLiveWorkoutZoneUpdate(zoneGroup, currentZoneDuration, previousZoneDuration); HKWorkout.zoneGroup(for:) and .zoneGroupsByType; HKWorkoutActivity.zoneGroup(for:); HKHealthStore.preferredWorkoutZoneConfiguration(for:); HKWorkoutBuilder.zoneConfiguration(for:) and setCustomZoneConfiguration(_:for:)
capabilities.resolution: Time-in-zone per workout, per quantity type — heart rate and cycling power.
capabilities.backfill: unknown; beta, assume forward-only for workouts recorded on iOS 27
capabilities.notes: iOS 27's only structural HealthKit addition beyond the two menopause category types. The complete iOS 27 beta delta in HealthKit is 45 symbols: this zones family, earliestAuthorizedSampleDate/getEarliestAuthorizedSampleDate, menopausalState, bleedingAfterMenopause and HKCategoryValueMenopausalState. Zero new HKQuantityTypeIdentifiers.

capabilities.stream: Background delivery, incremental sync and bucketed history — the collection mechanics
capabilities.api: HKObserverQuery(sampleType:predicate:updateHandler:) and (15.0+) HKObserverQuery(queryDescriptors:updateHandler:); HKHealthStore.enableBackgroundDelivery(for:frequency:) / disableBackgroundDelivery(for:) / disableAllBackgroundDelivery(); HKUpdateFrequency {.immediate, .hourly, .daily, .weekly}; HKAnchoredObjectQuery(type:predicate:anchor:limit:resultsHandler:) with .updateHandler and HKQueryAnchor (modern: HKAnchoredObjectQueryDescriptor); HKStatisticsCollectionQuery(quantityType:quantitySamplePredicate:options:anchorDate:intervalComponents:) with .statisticsUpdateHandler
capabilities.permission: the underlying types' read authorization only
capabilities.entitlement: com.apple.developer.healthkit.background-delivery (Boolean) is REQUIRED on iOS 15+ / watchOS 8+. Without it enableBackgroundDelivery fails with HKError.errorAuthorizationDenied. Xcode writes it automatically when you tick the HealthKit capability; it is NOT independently configurable in the App ID UI on the developer portal.
capabilities.minIOS: 8.0 for observer/anchored queries; the background-delivery entitlement requirement begins at 15.0; multi-descriptor observer queries 15.0
capabilities.resolution: FREQUENCY CAPS, verbatim from Apple: 'The system wakes your app at most once per time period defined by the specified frequency. Some sample types have a maximum frequency of hourly. The system enforces this frequency transparently. For example, on iOS, stepCount samples have an hourly maximum frequency.' On watchOS most types are hourly-capped and ONLY these ten may use .immediate: highHeartRateEvent, lowHeartRateEvent, irregularHeartRhythmEvent, environmentalAudioExposureEvent, headphoneAudioExposureEvent, lowCardioFitnessEvent, numberOfTimesFallen, vo2Max, handwashingEvent, toothbrushingEvent. On watchOS the budget is shared with WKApplicationRefreshBackgroundTask: four updates per hour, and only while your app has a complication on the active watch face.
capabilities.backfill: HKAnchoredObjectQuery with anchor = nil returns the ENTIRE history for the type in one pass — use `limit` and iterate, since an unbounded first sync of heartRate can be hundreds of thousands of samples. Subsequent runs with the saved HKQueryAnchor return only additions plus HKDeletedObject deletions; deletions are visible ONLY through anchored queries.
capabilities.notes: SUSPENDED APP: yes, the system relaunches your app in the background to deliver. REBOOT: registration persists — it is stored by the system, not your process. FORCE-QUIT: NO. Apple DTS, developer forums thread 803365: 'When the user force quits an app by swiping up in the multitasking UI, iOS... sets a flag that prevents the app from being launched in the background. That flag gets cleared when the user next launches the app manually... there's no documented way for your app to override the user's choice.' You MUST create all observer queries in application(_:didFinishLaunchingWithOptions:) — HealthKit fires update handlers immediately on launch and a query created later misses that delivery. You MUST call the HKObserverQueryCompletionHandler; three failures and HealthKit permanently stops delivering until you re-enable. Background delivery does NOT work in the Simulator. Use HKStatisticsCollectionQuery for 'daily steps for the last 5 years' — it applies Apple's cross-source deduplication that manual summing does not.

capabilities.stream: Authorization semantics — the write-blind read model
capabilities.api: HKHealthStore.requestAuthorization(toShare:read:); authorizationStatus(for:) -> HKAuthorizationStatus {.notDetermined, .sharingDenied, .sharingAuthorized}; getRequestStatusForAuthorization(toShare:read:) -> HKAuthorizationRequestStatus {.unknown, .shouldRequest, .unnecessary}; SwiftUI .healthDataAccessRequest(store:shareTypes:readTypes:trigger:completion:) from HealthKitUI; iOS 27 beta earliestAuthorizedSampleDate(for:) and getEarliestAuthorizedSampleDate(for:completion:); HKHealthStore.isHealthDataAvailable()
capabilities.permission: NSHealthShareUsageDescription AND NSHealthUpdateUsageDescription must BOTH be present or requestAuthorization throws. NSHealthClinicalHealthRecordsShareUsageDescription for clinical records. NSHealthRequiredReadAuthorizationTypeIdentifiers optional.
capabilities.resolution: The sheet groups types into categories (Activity, Heart, Nutrition...) with per-type read and share toggles.
capabilities.backfill: On first grant your app can read the ENTIRE history of granted types with no time limit. iOS 27 beta adds a second sheet: 'a second screen prompts them to choose how much historical data to grant your app, either a recent limited window or their full history.'
capabilities.notes: THE WRITE-BLIND RULE, verbatim: 'your app doesn't know whether someone granted or denied permission to read data from HealthKit. If they denied permission, attempts to read data from HealthKit return only samples that your app successfully saved to the HealthKit store.' authorizationStatus(for:) reports SHARE (write) status only and says nothing about reads. getRequestStatusForAuthorization tells you whether the sheet would appear, not what was granted. iOS 27, verbatim: 'HealthKit intentionally prevents your app from distinguishing between full access and denied access to specific types; both cases return no entry in the result dictionary. Limited authorization is the only authorization state your app can positively identify.' The sole exception to write-blindness is HKCharacteristicType, whose getters throw errorAuthorizationDenied. Also: Xcode adds `healthkit` to UIRequiredDeviceCapabilities when you enable the capability — delete that entry if you want the app installable on non-HealthKit devices.

blockers: Sleep Score (iOS 26 / watchOS 26) is NOT in HealthKit. Grepping the iOS 26.5 SDK for 'Score' yields only workoutEffortScore, estimatedWorkoutEffortScore, and the two scored-assessment identifiers. Apple computes Sleep Score from sleepAnalysis data third parties already have, but the score itself is Health-app-only with no API. You must reimplement it from duration, bedtime consistency and interruptions.

A whole class of Apple-computed derivations is Health-app-only with only the raw inputs exposed: AFib History percentages beyond the atrialFibrillationBurden sample, Cardio Fitness notification logic, Walking Steadiness notification thresholds, the Vitals app's outlier detection, Medications interaction warnings, and the wrist-temperature deviation-from-baseline that the Health app charts. HealthKit gives you atrialFibrillationBurden, vo2Max, appleWalkingSteadiness and appleSleepingWristTemperature — not Apple's interpretations of them.

You cannot detect read denial, ever. authorizationStatus(for:) is share-only. A denied type is byte-for-byte indistinguishable from a type with no data — both return an empty result set. Apple states this is intentional and there is no API that will change it. The only positively detectable state is iOS 27's limited-history window via earliestAuthorizedSampleDate.

Passing a per-object-authorization type (vision prescriptions) to requestAuthorization(toShare:read:) fails with HKError.errorInvalidArgument. It looks like an ordinary HKSampleType in every enumeration and is not. Use requestPerObjectReadAuthorization(for:predicate:), which re-prompts on every single call regardless of prior grants.

Background delivery does not survive a user force-quit (swipe-up in the app switcher). Confirmed by an Apple DTS engineer in developer forums thread 803365: iOS sets a flag blocking background launch until the user manually reopens the app. Not a bug, no override. It DOES survive reboot and ordinary system termination/suspension.

enableBackgroundDelivery hard-fails with errorAuthorizationDenied on iOS 15+ without com.apple.developer.healthkit.background-delivery in the signed entitlements. Xcode adds it with the HealthKit capability, but it is NOT a row in Apple's supported-capabilities-ios table and is not configurable in the App ID portal UI — so when a build system strips or desynchronises entitlements (a recurring failure with fastlane- and EAS-managed profiles) it fails silently at runtime, not at build time.

Clinical records require com.apple.developer.healthkit.access = ["health-records"] (the only legal value of that key) plus the separate NSHealthClinicalHealthRecordsShareUsageDescription Info.plist key. Apple's supported-capabilities-ios table lists 'HealthKit' and 'HealthKit Estimate Recalibration' as free-tier available but does NOT list Clinical Health Records at all, so free-personal-team signability for that one sub-capability is genuinely unestablished. Everything else in this domain runs on the base entitlement.

CONTESTED, both sides: Apple's supported-capabilities table defines its free column as 'Apple Account holders who have agreed to the Apple Developer Agreement... developers can't distribute apps' — that is not verbatim identical to an Xcode-managed personal team signing to a physical device, and I found no Apple document stating the personal-team entitlement set explicitly. FOR free-team viability: enabling the HealthKit capability in Xcode causes Xcode to write all three HealthKit entitlements (healthkit, healthkit.access, healthkit.background-delivery) into the provisioning profile allowlist, which is exactly the mechanism developers report in the fastlane/expo issue threads. AGAINST: those same threads document entitlement desync errors, and the background-delivery entitlement is invisible in the App ID configuration UI so there is no portal-side confirmation. Verdict: treat base HealthKit + background delivery as free-team-signable with high confidence; verify health-records empirically on device before designing around it.

Free personal-team provisioning profiles expire after 7 days. A self-installed quantified-self app relying on continuous background delivery will silently stop collecting one week after each install unless you re-sign on a schedule. This is a personal-team limitation, not a HealthKit one, but it defeats the entire use case if unplanned.

No iPhoneOS27.x SDK is publicly mirrored yet (xybp888/iOS-SDKs tops out at iPhoneOS26.5.sdk as of this research), so all iOS 27 claims here are derived from Apple's live DocC beta metadata (beta:true, introducedAt 27.0), not a header diff. The iOS 26.5 counts (120 / 70 / 6 / 2 / 2 / 1 / 9 / 84 / 71) are header-verified; the iOS 27 delta is docs-verified only.

HKActivitySummaryType, HKCharacteristicType and HKUserAnnotatedMedicationType are HKObjectType but NOT HKSampleType, so HKObserverQuery and enableBackgroundDelivery do not apply to any of them. You cannot be woken for a ring-goal change or for a new medication appearing in the user's list — only for HKMedicationDoseEvent samples.
HKDocumentQuery (CDA) is one-shot with no update handler, so there is no incremental-sync path for clinical documents.

Vision Pro Guest User sessions silently fail all authorization requests (the sheet is never shown) and reject all writes with errorNotPermissibleForGuestUserMode. Irrelevant on iPhone, but it is the one documented state where requestAuthorization fails with no visible error.
nonObvious: THREE readable category types exist in the SDK but appear nowhere in Apple's documentation navigation or DocC navigator index: HKCategoryTypeIdentifierSleepApneaEvent, HKCategoryTypeIdentifierBleedingDuringPregnancy, HKCategoryTypeIdentifierBleedingAfterPregnancy (all iOS 18.0 / watchOS 11.0). Their doc pages resolve only by direct URL. Any enumeration scraped from Apple's website — which is what nearly every published HealthKit list is — silently misses them. The only reliable enumeration source is HKTypeIdentifiers.h from a real SDK.

HKHeartbeatSeriesSample gives you sub-millisecond individual heartbeat timestamps with a precededByGap flag. HealthKit publishes only SDNN as a quantity type, but from the beat series you can compute RMSSD, pNN50, LF/HF, sample entropy — the entire HRV literature. Apple Watch only, base entitlement only, and it is absent from the Health app XML export. This is the single highest-leverage stream in the whole domain and most developers never touch it.

HKWorkoutRoute returns full-fidelity ~1 Hz CLLocation traces — latitude, longitude, altitude, speed, course, accuracy — for every outdoor workout ever recorded, with NO CoreLocation permission and no NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription. The coordinates come out of HealthKit, not Core Location, so the location-permission machinery never engages.

HKQuantitySeriesSampleQuery expands a single 'summary' quantity sample into its underlying high-frequency datum stream. Run only HKSampleQuery and you get pre-aggregated values; run the series query on the same samples and you get per-second cyclingPower, runningPower, underwaterDepth and more. Almost nobody does this.

HKAnchoredObjectQuery is the ONLY way to observe deletions. HKSampleQuery and HKStatisticsCollectionQuery cannot see HKDeletedObject at all, so a sync built on them accumulates ghost records forever when the user deletes data in the Health app.

Never sum step or distance samples across sources — HealthKit stores overlapping samples from iPhone and Watch simultaneously. HKStatisticsQuery and HKStatisticsCollectionQuery apply Apple's own cross-source deduplication; manual summation double-counts, sometimes by 2x on days the user carried both devices.

The 71 HKMetadataKey constants are a second, free data layer riding on samples you already read. HKMetadataKeyWasUserEntered separates sensors from typing. HKMetadataKeyBarometricPressure and WeatherCondition/Temperature/Humidity give ambient environment on every workout. HKMetadataKeyHeartRateMotionContext is the only reliable way to identify resting-context heart beats. HKMetadataKeyQuantityClampedToUpperBound/LowerBound flags values that hit a sensor ceiling and are therefore not real readings.

iOS 26 added an entire data family — HKMedicationDoseEvent + HKUserAnnotatedMedication + HKMedicationConcept — that requires only the base entitlement, despite being medication data. Crucially the system writes notInteracted rows for reminder slots the user never touched, so you get a true denominator for adherence rather than only the doses they bothered to log.

HKObserverQuery must be created inside application(_:didFinishLaunchingWithOptions:), not in a view controller or a task. HealthKit calls update handlers for pending deliveries the instant your app launches; a query registered a few hundred milliseconds later misses that delivery entirely, and because you must acknowledge deliveries, three misses permanently disable background delivery for that type.

watchOS .immediate background delivery is restricted to an explicit whitelist of exactly ten types (highHeartRateEvent, lowHeartRateEvent, irregularHeartRhythmEvent, environmentalAudioExposureEvent, headphoneAudioExposureEvent, lowCardioFitnessEvent, numberOfTimesFallen, vo2Max, handwashingEvent, toothbrushingEvent), and even then the app must have a complication on the active watch face and shares a 4-per-hour budget with WKApplicationRefreshBackgroundTask. Requesting .immediate for anything else silently degrades to hourly.

HKCharacteristicType is the only family where read denial is detectable — its getters throw errorAuthorizationDenied because there is no empty result set to hide behind. You can exploit this as a canary: if dateOfBirthComponents() throws, the user denied the whole Health sheet, which tells you something the sample APIs never will.

Correlations authorize per CHILD type, and correlation children ALSO appear as independent top-level samples. Request bloodPressure alone and you get nothing; query everything naively and you double-count every meal's calories and every blood-pressure reading.

HKActivitySummary carries the user's ring GOALS (activeEnergyBurnedGoal, exerciseTimeGoal, standHoursGoal), which are not derivable from any sample type. But HKActivitySummaryType is not an HKSampleType, so there is no background delivery for it, and its query needs an NSPredicate built on HKPredicateKeyPathDateComponents with an explicit NSCalendar carrying the right era and timezone — get the calendar wrong and you get zero results with no error.

EXPORT-ONLY DATA: the Health app's export.xml <Me> element carries HKCharacteristicTypeIdentifierCardioFitnessMedicationsUse, which has no counterpart anywhere in the HealthKit API — the SDK defines exactly six characteristic identifiers and this is not one of them. It is, as far as I can determine, the only datum genuinely obtainable ONLY via export.

THE EXPORT IS MOSTLY A DOWNGRADE, not a superset. Verified DTD (HealthKit Export Version 11, embedded at the top of export.xml, not fetched from a URL) defines: HealthData, ExportDate, Me, Record, Correlation, Workout, WorkoutEvent, WorkoutRoute, FileReference, ActivitySummary, MetadataEntry, HeartRateVariabilityMetadataList, InstantaneousBeatsPerMinute, ClinicalRecord, Audiogram, SensitivityPoint. Later shipping versions add WorkoutStatistics and WorkoutActivity (secondary sources; I could not obtain a post-v11 DTD verbatim). The ZIP also contains export_cda.xml, workout-routes/*.gpx and electrocardiograms/*.csv. What the API has and the export does NOT: HKHeartbeatSeriesSample (the export's InstantaneousBeatsPerMinute is only the HRV-sample summary list, not the full series), HKAttachment, HKStateOfMind, HKVisionPrescription, medications, scored assessments, HKDevice/HKSourceRevision structured provenance (flattened to sourceName/device strings), sample UUIDs, and per-quantity series expansion. ECG voltage becomes a CSV file, losing the HKElectrocardiogram object's classification/symptomsStatus linkage. Net: for a self-installed app the API is strictly richer than the export, with cardioFitnessMedicationsUse the lone exception.

The Apple Health export ZIP is not a stable contract — Apple bumps the embedded DTD version between iOS releases without documentation, and there are long-standing reports of the iOS 16-era export mislabelling endDate as startDate, plus an iOS 14 regression that produced valid-but-empty 438-byte GPX route files. Never build a pipeline that assumes the export is a reliable snapshot; the API is the durable interface.

HKAudiogramSensitivityPointClampingRange (iOS 18.1) tells you whether a hearing threshold was clipped at the test's floor or ceiling. Without checking it you will read an AirPods hearing-test result as a true threshold when it is actually a limit of the test.

iOS 27's earliestAuthorizedSampleDate is a behavioural change you must code defensively for even before it ships: Apple explicitly warns 'Avoid interpreting the absence of older samples as evidence they don't exist.' If your analytics assume a full history and the user grants a 3-month window, every trend you compute silently becomes wrong with no error surfaced.
